newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banks refuse finance for Gdansk shipyard.
newsitem.headline: Polish banks refuse finance for Gdansk shipyard.

text.p: A consortium of Polish banks on Tuesday dealt a blow to the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard's struggle for survival by refusing $100 million in credit to finance construction of five ships.

"Bank Gdanski SA announces that all the banks, invited to take part in a consortium to extend credit for a plan to build five ships by the bankrupt Stocznia Gdanska SA, gave a negative answer concerning the possibility of financing this project," the consortium's lead bank said in a statement.

The statement, issued to the Polish Securities Commission and reporters, said it would be too risky to get involved as the struggling shipyard's receiver had not met basic conditions for organising finance and ensuring the project succeeded.
"Only if the receiver meets conditions earlier announced by the banks can there be a chance that the banks will again examine the possibility of financing this project," it said.

The Baltic coast yard, cradle of the Solidarity trade union which overthrew communism in 1989, was declared bankrupt last year after its debts reached 415 million zlotys and banks refused to credit its further operations.
Because the yard still had unfilled orders, part of the shipyard's assets and workforce were hived off to a new, debt-free New Gdansk Shipyard company to complete the contracts.

On January 15 the new yard signed a contract with Germany's Schoeller Holding Ltd for the construction of five container ships worth $27.5 million each, but it still needed to persuade banks to finance their construction.

Gdanski had said the seven-bank group, examining the possibility of extending around $100 million in credit, first wanted the New Gdansk yard to boost its capital, because government guarantees did not cover the full scope of the loan.

They also wanted the yard to re-negotiate deadlines for the first two ships and insisted that the contracts for the construction of the ships be transferred from the bankrupt Gdansk shipyard to the new yard.
The banks also wanted a realistic plan of changes in the functioning and organisation of the bankrupt Gdansk Shipyard.

The banks' decision appeared to be a blow to the yard, as the government says it will not even consider extending guarantees for credit to build the ships unless commercial banks first agree to extend such credit.
